purpose: Test whether one source-only catalog-level astrometric uncertainty reconciles the Abell 2146 spectroscopic coordinates with the frozen HSC/NSC candidate excess, then propagate the resulting candidate/null posterior, HST F814W luminosity availability, and quoted redshift errors into a deterministic luminosity-current ensemble without choosing hard counterparts or reading lensing, halo, or gravity targets.

population.candidate_inventory_role: These aggregate facts were already exposed by V19Y/V19AA. They verify inventory only and do not select the astrometric width or a counterpart.

catalog_level_astrometric_calibration.question: Does one additional publication-to-HST centroid scatter, shared by all 63 Abell 2146 members, predict the source-only candidate offsets better than the V19AA quantization-plus-0.1-arcsec control?
catalog_level_astrometric_calibration.coordinate_model: the unchanged V19AA decimal-degree rounding rectangle convolved with candidate astrometric uncertainty and one additional isotropic Gaussian sigma_extra
catalog_level_astrometric_calibration.candidate_density_equation: f_mi(sigma_extra)=the V19AA uniform rounding-rectangle density convolved with the candidate Gaussian at the measured east/north offset
catalog_level_astrometric_calibration.primary_selection: maximize the summed source-only log evidence at q=0.9; ties choose the smaller sigma_extra

cross_validation.assignment: sort members by numeric object_id and assign index modulo 7
cross_validation.within_fold_rule: select sigma_extra on the other six folds and score the held-out fold against the sigma_extra=0 control

catalog_level_astrometric_calibration.interpretation: sigma_extra is a catalog measurement nuisance shared by this published table, not a gravitational constant, physical smoothing scale, galaxy size, cluster parameter, or Sigma wavelength

luminosity_and_current.photometry_source: the exact HSC V3 summary A_F814W value attached to the sampled unified candidate's frozen hsc_match_id
luminosity_and_current.missing_rule: A sampled null state or candidate without finite HSC F814W remains missing_photometry; do not infer a luminosity from the spectroscopic selection limit or another member.
luminosity_and_current.cluster_systemic_cz: median heliocentric cz over all 63 spectroscopic members, recomputed in every draw after perturbing every row by its quoted Gaussian cz uncertainty
luminosity_and_current.claim: candidate-marginalized relative F814W line-of-sight luminosity-current proxy, not stellar mass or a three-dimensional current

null_position_model.conditional_distribution: uniform in east and north over the original V19AA decimal-degree rounding rectangle
null_position_model.interpretation: The null state retains the spectroscopic galaxy and measured velocity but has no identified catalog luminosity.

ensemble.state_sampling: draw each member independently from its exact candidate/null posterior because the frozen Abell candidate inventory contains no candidate shared between members
ensemble.redshift_sampling: independent Gaussian using each catalogued cz uncertainty
ensemble.null_sampling: sample a fresh coordinate from the frozen rounding rectangle
ensemble.row_rule: all 63 spectroscopic members appear in every draw; luminosity/current fields are blank only when the sampled state has missing photometry

gates.failure_rule: Fail closed without extending the sigma grid, changing q, selecting a width from coverage or photometry, forcing a candidate, assigning luminosity to a null state, changing the ensemble size or seed, or reading lensing, halo, or gravity targets.

claim_boundary: V19BB tests and propagates a catalog measurement uncertainty; it does not fit a gravitational length or an object-specific physics parameter.
The primary width is selected without HSC magnitude, lensing, halo, gravity residual, published subcluster label, BCG flag, or spectral type.
A finite F814W flux is a relative luminosity proxy, not stellar mass, total baryonic mass, or a fitted mass-to-light ratio.
Null and missing-F814W states remain explicit and contribute no invented luminosity.
Only line-of-sight velocity is measured; transverse currents remain unmeasured.
Passing would supply the Abell collisionless input needed for a matched two-cluster source test, not evidence for the long-wavelength gravity hypothesis.
